title: Activate DHM Reviews: An Honest Look at the Canadian Hangover Pill
excerpt: An independent Activate DHM review: what's in the Canadian hangover capsule, what its Health Canada licence means, what users say, and how it stacks up to bigger DHM brands.
metaDescription: Activate DHM reviews: what's in this Canadian DHM supplement, what Health Canada approval means, user sentiment, and how it stacks up to bigger DHM brands.
author: DHM Guide Team
content:
**The honest verdict first:** Activate DHM is a small Canadian hangover supplement from a Winnipeg company (Bomb Squad Nutrition Ltd.). It combines DHM (dihydromyricetin) with N-acetyl cysteine (NAC), B vitamins, milk thistle and electrolytes, and it carries a Health Canada licence as a liver protectant. On paper the formula is sensible: every ingredient is one you'll find in better-known hangover products. The problem is what we couldn't confirm. In the brand's own marketing and the press coverage we reviewed, we did not find the milligram amount of DHM or any other ingredient per capsule, and there is very little independent customer feedback outside sponsored articles and the brand's social channels. Without the dose, nobody can tell you whether two capsules give you a meaningful amount of DHM or a token one.

**Who it suits:** Canadians who want a locally made, Health Canada-licensed product, ship it free in Canada, and are willing to check the label for the DHM amount before buying. **Who should look elsewhere:** anyone in the US (it's sold in Canada), anyone who wants the DHM dose stated up front, and anyone comparing value per milligram. Larger single-ingredient DHM brands print their dose clearly, which makes them easier to judge.

We don't sell Activate DHM and we don't earn anything from it. There's no store link on this page. This review is based on the brand's public claims, press coverage, and the published research on its ingredients.

> **This is not medical advice.** Hangover supplements are not a way to drink safely, and nothing in a capsule offsets the risks of heavy drinking. DHM, NAC and milk thistle can interact with some medicines, and none of them have been well studied in pregnancy. **Talk to a doctor or pharmacist before using any of these supplements if** you take prescription medicines (especially blood thinners, diabetes medicines, or drugs metabolized by the liver), you have liver or kidney disease, you are pregnant or breastfeeding, or you are using supplements because you drink most days. If you're worried about how much you drink, your doctor is a good first call.

## What Is Activate DHM?

Activate DHM is a capsule supplement made in Canada by Bomb Squad Nutrition Ltd., a start-up based in Winnipeg, Manitoba. It launched around early 2022, with local and national Canadian outlets covering the launch that spring. Much of that early coverage (on sites such as ChrisD.ca, Narcity and Curiocity) was clearly labelled as sponsored content, which is worth knowing when you weigh the glowing tone.

The brand sells mainly through its own website and describes the product as:

- A **"2-step system"**: one capsule with your first drink, and one before bed with a big glass of water. Sponsored articles also mention taking two before bed after a bigger night.
- Built around **DHM**, the active compound extracted from the Japanese raisin tree (*Hovenia dulcis*).
- Rounded out with **NAC, a B-vitamin complex, milk thistle and electrolytes**.
- **All-natural, vegan, gluten-free and nut-free**, according to the brand and its press.
- **Health Canada approved as a liver protectant**, and described in sponsored coverage as the first Canadian product licensed to use DHM.

The brand has offered free shipping within Canada, a discount code on its homepage, and a money-back guarantee on a first order. Those terms change, so check the site directly.

### What "Health Canada approved" actually means

This is the claim that sets Activate apart from most American DHM brands, so it's worth understanding.

In Canada, supplements are regulated as **natural health products**. Before one can be sold, the company has to get a product licence, and the licensed product gets an eight-digit **Natural Product Number (NPN)** printed on the label. To get that licence, the company submits information on the ingredients, the dose, the quality standards and the health claim it wants to make. Health Canada reviews it and decides which claims are allowed.

That's a real step up from the US, where a supplement can go on sale without any pre-market review at all. It means a licensed Canadian product has a reviewed ingredient list, a defined dose, and approved wording on the label.

What it does **not** mean is that Health Canada tested the product and found it prevents hangovers. Natural health product claims can be supported by traditional use or by modest evidence, not the large clinical trials required for a drug. "Approved as a liver protectant" means the claim wording was accepted for that ingredient at that dose. It isn't a finding that the capsule protects your liver from alcohol.

One useful side effect of the Canadian system: because the dose is part of the licence, every licensed product is listed in Health Canada's public **Licensed Natural Health Products Database (LNHPD)**. You can search it by product or company name and see the medicinal ingredients and the amount of each per dose. If you're seriously considering Activate DHM, that's the single best way to see exactly how much DHM you'd be getting.

## Activate DHM Ingredients: What Each One Does

Here's what the evidence says about each ingredient the brand lists. We've deliberately avoided guessing the doses, because we couldn't verify them.

### DHM (dihydromyricetin)

DHM is the main reason people buy this product, and the reason the brand is named after it.

The best-known research comes from animal studies. A 2012 study in the *Journal of Neuroscience* (Shen and colleagues, at UCLA) found that DHM reduced signs of alcohol intoxication and withdrawal in rats, and appeared to work at GABA-A receptors in the brain, the same receptors alcohol acts on. Later work from a University of Southern California group, including a 2020 study in *Alcoholism: Clinical and Experimental Research*, reported that DHM reduced alcohol-related liver injury in mice and appeared to speed up the breakdown of alcohol and acetaldehyde (the toxic by-product that drives many hangover symptoms).

The weak spot is human evidence. There are only a handful of small human studies, many of them on combination products, and some funded by supplement makers. They suggest DHM may help some people feel somewhat better the next day, but nothing yet shows it reliably prevents hangovers or protects the human liver from alcohol. We go through the trials one by one in our [review of DHM randomized controlled trials](/never-hungover/dhm-randomized-controlled-trials) and our [honest look at whether DHM works](/never-hungover/does-dhm-work-honest-science-review-2025).

**Why the dose matters:** most single-ingredient DHM products on the market provide roughly 300 mg per capsule, and common use is in the range of 300 to 600 mg or more per drinking session, depending on body size and how much you drink. Our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025) explains where those numbers come from. Because Activate packs five ingredient types into a capsule, there's less room for DHM than in a capsule that contains only DHM. It may still be a reasonable amount, but you can't know without the label.

### NAC (N-acetyl cysteine)

NAC is a building block your body uses to make **glutathione**, the main antioxidant the liver uses to neutralize toxic by-products, including acetaldehyde from alcohol. It's also the hospital antidote for acetaminophen (Tylenol) overdose, which is a different use at much higher doses.

For hangovers, the human evidence is limited to a few small studies with mixed results, and some research suggests NAC works better if it's taken before or during drinking rather than the morning after. It's a reasonable inclusion. It's not a proven hangover fix. Our [NAC vs DHM comparison](/never-hungover/nac-vs-dhm-which-antioxidant-better-liver-protection-2025) covers this in more depth.

### Milk thistle

Milk thistle (its active compounds are called silymarin) is one of the oldest liver supplements around and appears in many hangover formulas. It has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects in lab studies. In people, though, systematic reviews of milk thistle for alcohol-related liver disease have not found clear benefits on hard outcomes. There's no good evidence that it prevents hangovers. It's generally well tolerated, which is why brands include it, but treat it as a supporting ingredient rather than a reason to buy.

### B vitamins

Alcohol can lower levels of several B vitamins, especially in people who drink heavily over time. A small 1970s study and later survey data have linked B vitamins to milder hangovers, but the evidence is thin. B vitamins are cheap and low-risk at normal doses. They're unlikely to make a noticeable difference after one night out if you eat a normal diet.

### Electrolytes

Alcohol makes you urinate more, and you lose some sodium and potassium along the way. The amount of electrolytes that fits in a capsule is small compared with a sports drink or oral rehydration solution. The brand's advice to take the second capsule with a big glass of water is probably doing more of the work here than the electrolytes in the capsule.

## What Activate DHM Users Say

This is a "reviews" page, so here's an honest summary of what we could find.

**Most visible praise comes from sponsored or brand-controlled sources.** The launch articles that describe Canadians who "swear by" the product, or call it a "life saver," were paid placements. The brand's own website and Instagram carry testimonials, as every brand's do. That doesn't make them false, but it does mean they're selected.

**Independent reviews are scarce.** Unlike the large DHM brands, Activate isn't a major Amazon seller with hundreds or thousands of verified-purchase ratings, and we didn't find substantial independent discussion of it on forums. That's typical for a small regional brand, not a red flag in itself. It just means there isn't much unbiased user sentiment to report.

**What positive testimonials tend to describe** is the same pattern people report with DHM products generally: waking up clearer, with less of the "hangxiety" or anxious, foggy feeling after a night out. **What we'd expect from the more cautious users**, based on how DHM products are reviewed generally, is that results vary and that it doesn't help much after very heavy drinking. No supplement does.

If you're reading reviews of Activate DHM elsewhere, a few checks help:

- Look for a "sponsored," "partner" or "advertorial" label at the top of the article.
- Prefer reviews that mention how much the person drank and what they compared it to.
- Be wary of any review, ours included, that calls a supplement a "cure." The US FDA sent warning letters to several hangover-product companies in 2020 for claiming their supplements could prevent or cure hangovers, because those are disease-type claims that supplements can't legally make.

## Activate DHM vs Bigger DHM Brands

How does a small, Canadian, multi-ingredient product compare with the larger DHM brands most readers already know? Here's the trade-off in plain terms.

| | Activate DHM | Double Wood DHM | No Days Wasted DHM Detox |
|---|---|---|---|
| Type | Multi-ingredient blend | Single-ingredient DHM | Multi-ingredient blend |
| Key ingredients | DHM, NAC, B vitamins, milk thistle, electrolytes | DHM only | DHM plus supporting ingredients |
| DHM per capsule clearly stated in marketing? | Not in the materials we reviewed | Yes (300 mg per capsule) | Listed on the product label |
| Regulatory status | Health Canada licensed (NPN) | US dietary supplement | US dietary supplement |
| Where sold | Mainly the brand's own site, Canada | Amazon and brand site, US | Amazon and brand site, US |
| Independent review volume | Low | High (over 1,000 Amazon ratings at last check) | Moderate (hundreds of Amazon ratings at last check) |

### The case for Activate

- **A licensed product.** The NPN means the ingredient list and dose went through a regulatory review, which most US DHM brands never face.
- **Made in Canada, shipped in Canada.** For Canadian buyers, ordering from a US Amazon listing can mean slow shipping, duties or simply no availability. Activate avoids that.
- **A sensible formula.** DHM plus NAC plus milk thistle is close to what many established brands sell.
- **Simple directions.** One capsule early, one before bed is easy to remember.

### The case against Activate

- **The DHM dose isn't easy to find.** This is the big one. You can't compare value or effectiveness without it.
- **Little independent feedback.** Most of what's out there was paid for or posted by the brand.
- **Blend trade-offs.** A capsule that holds five kinds of ingredients usually holds less of each than a single-ingredient product. If DHM is the part you care about, a dedicated DHM capsule gives you more of it per pill.
- **Limited availability outside Canada.**

### If you'd rather use a well-known DHM brand

If you're in the US, or you want the DHM dose printed plainly on the label, two of the brands we've reviewed in depth are reasonable places to start.

**Double Wood DHM** is the simplest option: 300 mg of DHM per capsule and nothing else, with one of the largest bodies of independent reviews in the category. It's a good choice if you want to control your own DHM dose and add other things (like NAC or electrolytes) separately. See our full [Double Wood DHM review](/never-hungover/double-wood-dhm-review-analysis), or [check the current price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20).

**No Days Wasted DHM Detox** is closer to Activate in spirit: a DHM-led blend with supporting ingredients, aimed at people who want one product rather than a stack. It costs more per serving than plain DHM. Read our [No Days Wasted review](/never-hungover/no-days-wasted-dhm-review-analysis), or [check the current price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20).

If you want a side-by-side of those two, we compare them directly in [Double Wood vs No Days Wasted](/never-hungover/double-wood-vs-no-days-wasted-dhm-comparison-2025). We also have reviews of other blends, including [Cheers Restore](/never-hungover/cheers-restore-review), and an honest look at a different approach altogether in our [ZBiotics review](/never-hungover/zbiotics-review).

## How to Take Activate DHM (and DHM Generally)

The brand's directions are one capsule with or before your first drink and one before bed with a large glass of water. That timing lines up with how most DHM brands suggest using their products: some before or during drinking, and some before sleep.

A few practical points apply to any DHM product, Activate included:

1. **Read the label for the DHM amount** and compare it with the ranges in our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025). If two capsules add up to much less DHM than other products use, that's worth knowing before you judge whether it "works."
2. **Timing matters more than people expect.** Our [DHM timing guide](/never-hungover/when-to-take-dhm-timing-guide-2025) explains why taking it earlier in the evening is the usual advice.
3. **Don't double up on blends.** If you combine Activate with another hangover product, check for overlapping ingredients like NAC, milk thistle and B vitamins.
4. **Water, food and sleep still do most of the work.** No capsule replaces eating before you drink, pacing yourself, and alternating with water.
5. **Count your drinks, not your capsules.** Feeling better the next morning is not the same as your body handling more alcohol safely. Your liver still has to process every drink.

## Safety: Who Should Be Careful

The ingredients in Activate DHM are generally well tolerated in healthy adults at normal supplement doses, but "natural" doesn't mean free of risk.

- **Medicines processed by the liver.** DHM has shown effects on liver enzymes in lab studies, and milk thistle may affect how some drugs are broken down. If you take prescription medicines, ask a pharmacist before adding any of these. Our [DHM medication interactions guide](/never-hungover/dhm-medication-interactions-safety-guide-2025) covers the main ones.
- **Blood thinners and diabetes medicines.** These are the categories where pharmacists most often advise caution with herbal liver supplements. Don't start one without checking.
- **Pregnancy and breastfeeding.** There isn't enough safety data on DHM in pregnancy. Avoid it unless a doctor says otherwise. (And in pregnancy, alcohol itself is the main concern.)
- **Allergy to the daisy family.** Milk thistle is related to ragweed, daisies and marigolds, and can cause reactions in people sensitive to those plants.
- **Heavy, daily drinking.** If you're reaching for a hangover pill most mornings, the supplement is not the issue to solve. A doctor can help, and there's no judgment in asking. Our [DHM safety guide](/never-hungover/dhm-safety-complete-guide-2025) covers the broader picture.

## Our Verdict on Activate DHM

Activate DHM looks like an honest attempt at a hangover supplement from a small Canadian company. The ingredients are sensible, the Health Canada licence is a genuine point in its favour, and the directions are simple. We have no reason to think it's a bad product.

But we can't call it a better product either, for two reasons we've been open about. First, the DHM amount per capsule wasn't stated in any of the marketing or coverage we reviewed, so we can't compare it on the one ingredient the brand is named after. Second, most of the positive feedback out there is sponsored or brand-hosted, and there's very little independent user sentiment to weigh.

**Our recommendation:** if you're in Canada and like the idea of a locally licensed product, look up its listing in Health Canada's Licensed Natural Health Products Database (or the label itself) and check the DHM amount per dose. If it lands in the same range as established products, it's a reasonable choice. If you're in the US, or you'd rather have a clear DHM dose and a large pool of independent reviews, a better-known brand is the easier, more transparent pick.

Whatever you choose, keep expectations realistic. The research on DHM is promising, mostly from animal studies, and no supplement reliably prevents a hangover after heavy drinking.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is Activate DHM legit?**

Activate DHM is a real product from Bomb Squad Nutrition Ltd., a Winnipeg company, and it carries a Health Canada natural health product licence (an NPN) with an approved liver-protectant claim. That means its ingredients, dose and label wording went through a regulatory review. It doesn't mean Health Canada tested it for hangover prevention. Much of the glowing press coverage was sponsored, and independent reviews are limited.

**What's in Activate DHM?**

According to the brand and its press coverage, Activate DHM contains DHM (dihydromyricetin), N-acetyl cysteine (NAC), a B-vitamin complex, milk thistle and electrolytes. It's marketed as vegan, gluten-free and nut-free. The milligram amount of each ingredient wasn't stated in the marketing we reviewed, so check the product label or Health Canada's Licensed Natural Health Products Database before buying.

**How much DHM is in Activate DHM?**

We couldn't confirm it from the brand's marketing or the press coverage. Because Activate is a licensed Canadian natural health product, the amount of DHM per dose is part of its licence and should appear on the label and in Health Canada's public database. For comparison, single-ingredient DHM products commonly provide about 300 mg per capsule.

**How do you take Activate DHM?**

The brand's directions are one capsule with or before your first drink and a second capsule before bed with a big glass of water. Sponsored coverage also mentions taking two before bed after a bigger night. Follow the directions on your package, and talk to a pharmacist first if you take prescription medicines.

**Is Activate DHM better than Double Wood or No Days Wasted?**

Not clearly. Activate has the advantage of a Health Canada licence and Canadian availability. Double Wood states its DHM dose plainly (300 mg per capsule) and has far more independent reviews, and No Days Wasted is a similar DHM-led blend with a larger US review base. Which is better for you depends mainly on where you live and how much DHM each serving actually provides.

**Can you buy Activate DHM in the US or on Amazon?**

Activate DHM has been sold mainly through its own website and marketed as sold in Canada. We didn't find it as a major Amazon listing. US buyers will generally find well-known DHM brands easier to get.

**Does Activate DHM prevent hangovers?**

No supplement reliably prevents hangovers, and supplements aren't allowed to claim they do. DHM has promising research, mostly in animals, and a few small human studies suggest some people feel better the next day. Results vary, and heavy drinking will still cause a hangover. The most reliable prevention is drinking less, eating first, and drinking water.

**Is Activate DHM safe?**

Its ingredients are generally well tolerated by healthy adults at normal supplement doses. Talk to a doctor or pharmacist first if you take prescription medicines (especially blood thinners or diabetes medicines), have liver or kidney disease, are pregnant or breastfeeding, or are allergic to plants in the daisy family, which includes milk thistle.
